summary: ADV-D094-02, ADV-D094-03, and D094-SF-1 are materially landed: the venue and selected runner class are now the same documented public-repository GitHub-hosted offering; the repository is PUBLIC; current resource figures match the cited table; the 2018 Mac-mini recital and stale last-Intel claim are withdrawn; and the native check handles 1, 0, ENOENT, and unexpected errors safely. ADV-D094-01 is not fully landed. GitHub-hosted labels identify mutable pools that provision a new VM per job, and runner images update regularly. D-094 still calls those labels `one machine` and `exact pins`, permits the actual image build to be selected only at execution, and fixes the image only within a sample window. That is not the promised exact one-machine/image identity and leaves cross-run threshold reproducibility and same-family drift undefined. A separate audit defect also records the frozen Codex turn-1 verdict as `OBJECT`; its actual verdict is `OBJECTIONS`. Until both are repaired, G03/G04 remain reserved, condition 4 remains 16 of 18 and PARTLY MET, and CONSENT is unavailable.

objections.title: The supposed exact pins are floating hosted-runner fleets and defer the actual image identity
objections.finding: The scoped D-006 successor validly changes the resource class and product-signs the public GitHub-hosted venues, but it does not deliver the repair it claims for ADV-D094-01. A workflow label such as `macos-15` or `ubuntu-24.04` selects a pool; GitHub provisions a new VM for each job. The subject names no stable host/CPU SKU and no selectable runner-image build. It explicitly says the first harness run records the live image build and fixes the image only during that sample window. Thus the actual VM and image identity remain execution-time values, and a same-label image-build or host-SKU change is not clearly covered by the listed successor triggers. Calling this `one machine per platform` and `exact pins` does not make it so.
objections.evidence: GitHub's current hosted-runner reference says each hosted runner (outside the single-CPU exception) is a new VM and gives resource classes rather than stable machine identities: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners . GitHub's runner-images repository states that images are typically deployed weekly: https://github.com/actions/runner-images . D-094 says `OS ... as shipped on that image`, defers the live image build to the first harness run, and only forbids unattended updates during the sample window. That is an audit trail for drift, not a pre-execution exact pin or a cross-run reproducibility rule.
objections.impact: D-086's G03/G04 reservation precondition remains unmet under the repair as represented. Startup percentiles and memory observations can move with opaque host SKU or same-family image changes while the file-08 cells falsely say exact pins landed. The proposed 18/18 and condition-4 MET edits would therefore run ahead of their premise.
objections.requiredRepair: Choose one of two honest routes and refreeze. Route A: use genuinely fixed/self-hosted machine and image identities that can be selected again. Route B: explicitly supersede D-006's exact-machine/exact-OS requirement with a hosted-fleet-class measurement contract; stop calling labels one machine or immutable exact pins; define a fail-closed preflight for label, architecture, CPU count and SKU/brand, RAM, storage, OS/build, and image version; define which same-label changes require a reviewed successor; and define how percentile samples and release-to-release regression comparisons remain valid across fresh VMs and image rollouts. Until that successor contract is complete, retain the reserved prefixes, 16 of 18, and PARTLY MET.

objections.title: The predecessor ledger misstates the Codex turn-1 verdict word
objections.finding: The turn-2 subject says `Codex OBJECT, 3 MUST-FIX`. The frozen Codex turn-1 verdict at the exact digest cited in the same subject has `verdict: OBJECTIONS`, with three MUST-FIX findings. `OBJECT` is the freeze-precondition stop verdict used when bytes move; that did not happen in turn 1.
